target_customer: School and public libraries, and librarians who manage cataloguing, circulation, inventory and grants
problem: Librarians spend time on tedious administrative tasks such as inventory, vendor ordering and grant applications that take them away from patrons.
business_model: B2B software subscription: library management system plus paid AI add-ons
product_category: AI-native integrated library system and library operations agents

founders.name: Carl-Hugo Jacobsson
founders.background_notes: YC page gives only a tagline; no background found.

founders.name: Kaan Sirin
founders.background_notes: YC page tagline 'chief librarian'; no background found.

competitors.name: Follett Destiny
competitors.what: Dominant K-12 library management system, adding Destiny AI tools
competitors.traction_then: Says 800+ US school districts use its AI features (vendor claim)

competitors.name: ibl.ai
competitors.what: AI library agent that plugs into existing library systems via API

technical_complexity.rationale: A full library management system with cataloguing, circulation and OPAC plus data migration is substantial engineering, and the AI features (spine reading, vendor comparison) are standard applied AI.

defensibility.rationale: Library systems hold catalog data and are painful to replace, which creates switching costs, but Follett already has the installed base.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Follett launched Destiny AI in February 2026 and bundled AI at no extra charge from August 2026, directly absorbing part of the wedge.

market_need_then: Librarians have heavy administrative workloads and school libraries rely on aging systems; Follett's own AI launch in 2026 shows incumbents saw demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses ossus.com, apparently the exact name .com; acquisition details not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Measured, civic and mission driven; frames libraries as infrastructure and says AI handles routine work while humans keep judgment

rebrands.why: A profile says it widened scope beyond school libraries; the school product keeps the name Librar

brand_strength.rationale: Newly renamed with no brand press found; the company keeps Librar as the school product name.

pivots.from: AI library system for school libraries (Librar Labs)
pivots.to: Intelligence for cultural institutions, starting with school and public libraries (Ossus)
pivots.why: Widen products beyond school libraries, per a secondary profile

outcome_analysis: Ossus, formerly Librar Labs, is an active Winter 2026 company reported to have raised a $6M seed and renamed in 2026 to widen beyond school libraries. The risk is that Follett, which dominates K-12 library software, bundled AI into Destiny, so Ossus must win through public libraries and better add-ons.
notes: The $6M seed appears in Distill and Nordic9 (lead Norrsken VC) but no primary announcement was found, and dates conflict (March 2026 on Nordic9, June 2026 elsewhere), so the round date is given as 2026. Caplight lists $7.5M total and CB Insights lists $500K total with YC and Wave Ventures; Dealroom lists a $125k seed. These conflicting figures are unverified. YC page lists a former founder, Jonathan Goertz (Founder/CEO), not included as a current founder. Founder backgrounds were not found. The founding year is not stated in sources. Outcome search found no acquisition or shutdown.
